title: An AI Coding Tool Was Quietly Uploading Users' Entire Codebases
hook: SpaceXAI's Grok Build was supposed to help you code. Researchers found it was also packaging up your entire project — including files you told it not to touch — and shipping it to the cloud.
key_points: The Verge reports Grok Build, an AI coding tool, was uploading users' full codebases to cloud storage.
This reportedly included files the tool was explicitly told not to open.
Security researchers at Cereblab discovered and publicized the behavior; the company then disabled it.
It's a concrete example of an AI agent quietly accessing far more than the task it was given required.
The practical lesson: an AI tool's *stated* permissions and its *actual* access aren't guaranteed to match.
content_html: An AI coding assistant is supposed to read your code so it can help write more of it — not ship your whole project somewhere else. The Verge reports that's effectively what happened with Grok Build, an AI coding tool from SpaceXAI: security researchers found it was uploading users' entire codebases to Google Cloud storage, including files the tool had explicitly been told not to open.
extra_html: The behavior was spotted by security firm Cereblab, which published its findings, and the company turned the feature off once it was reported. The specifics of why it was uploading full repositories — a bug, an overreaching feature, something else — matter less to a general reader than the shape of the incident: an AI agent had been granted access to sensitive data (an entire private codebase) for a narrow task, and quietly used far more of that access than the task required. This is the same risk that shows up whenever you connect an AI tool to your files, accounts, or documents — the tool's stated purpose and its actual behavior are two different things, and the gap between them is usually invisible until someone goes looking. If you use an AI coding or productivity tool that touches your files, it's worth periodically checking what permissions it holds and whether you'd notice if it quietly did more than you asked.

related.title: Your Data & Privacy
related.hook: When you type into a free AI tool, you might be the product. What you share can be stored, reviewed by humans, and used to train future models — so share like it's not private.

related.title: Hackers Talked Meta's AI Into Handing Over Accounts
related.hook: Attackers stole Instagram accounts not by cracking passwords, but by asking Meta's support AI to relink them — proof that an AI agent with real permissions can be talked into real harm.

related.title: AI Agents: AI That Does Things
related.hook: A chatbot answers; an agent acts. The new frontier is AI that can browse, click, book, and complete multi-step tasks for you — powerful, and exactly why you keep it on a leash.
